nodes.label: Prisma CLI AI Safety Checkpoint
nodes.author: prisma
nodes.rationale: Prisma blocks destructive commands (migrate reset, db push --force-reset/--accept-data-loss) when it detects an AI agent, requiring explicit user consent captured via PRISMA_USER_CONSENT_FOR_DANGEROUS_AI_ACTION to prevent accidental data loss from agent automation.

nodes.label: Runtime Host and Port Binding Rules
nodes.author: prisma
nodes.norm_label: runtime host and port binding rules
nodes.rationale: Deployed servers must bind on 0.0.0.0 (not localhost/127.0.0.1) and listen on process.env.PORT, because Compute readiness only checks listening ports and a loopback-only listener can appear ready while unreachable from public ingress.

nodes.label: Preserve Original Database Error Code/Message
nodes.author: prisma
nodes.rationale: Wrap driver failures in DriverAdapterError preserving originalCode/originalMessage so Prisma can surface a useful P2039 fallback for unmapped errors instead of losing diagnostic detail.

nodes.label: Savepoints Live on Transaction Not Adapter-Global Depth
nodes.author: prisma
nodes.norm_label: savepoints live on transaction not adapter-global depth
nodes.rationale: Keeping nested transaction/savepoint state on the shared adapter breaks under parallel transactions; state must be connection-local to the returned Transaction object.

nodes.label: MongoDB Has No Prisma v7 Connector
nodes.author: prisma
nodes.norm_label: mongodb has no prisma v7 connector
nodes.rationale: Prisma v7 never ships a MongoDB connector; v6 is the terminal classic-ORM major for MongoDB, so MongoDB projects must either stay on v6 or migrate to Prisma Next rather than 'upgrading to v7'.

nodes.label: Use Direct Connection String, Not Pooled/Accelerate
nodes.author: prisma
nodes.norm_label: use direct connection string, not pooled/accelerate
nodes.rationale: Use endpoints.direct.connectionString for new projects; pooled/accelerate endpoints are legacy Accelerate-specific and unnecessary for new setups.

nodes.label: Caveman Auto-Clarity Rule
nodes.rationale: Drop caveman compression during security warnings, irreversible actions, and multi-step sequences to avoid misread from ambiguity introduced by compression.

nodes.label: Ponytail Decision Ladder (YAGNI-first)
nodes.rationale: Stop at the first rung that holds: question existence, reuse existing code, use stdlib, use native platform features, use installed deps, one line, minimum code — favors least code that solves the real problem.

nodes.label: Ponytail: When NOT to be Lazy
nodes.norm_label: ponytail: when not to be lazy
nodes.rationale: Never simplify away input validation at trust boundaries, error handling preventing data loss, security, accessibility, or explicitly requested features — laziness must not compromise correctness or safety.
